state_program_name: Assisted Living Facility (ALF) licensed by AHCA under Ch. 429 Part I, F.S. and rule chapter 59A-36, F.A.C. (specialty licenses: ECC, LNS, LMH)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Assisted Living Facility (ALF) in Florida. The facility is licensed by the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) under Chapter 429, Part I, Florida Statutes, and rule chapter 59A-36, Florida Administrative Code. If the facility holds a specialty license (Extended Congregate Care (ECC), Limited Nursing Services (LNS) or Limited Mental Health (LMH)), the manual also covers the additional requirements of that license.

The manual does the following:

- Turns Florida's licensing requirements into written policies and step-by-step procedures that staff can follow every day.
- Gives owners, the administrator, managers and staff one consistent reference for resident admission, care, rights, medications, staffing, training, food service, finances, records, and emergency management.
- Shows AHCA surveyors, county emergency management and fire and health inspectors, residents and their representatives that the facility has written policies where the rules call for them.
- Supports resident safety, dignity, choice and quality of care.

The manual is a working document. It is not legal advice and does not replace the statutes and rules. If the manual and the law differ, the law controls.

### Required customization, adoption, currency and training

- **Customize it.** This manual is a template. Before use, replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed item with the facility's own name, licensed capacity, license type(s), staff titles, telephone numbers, and local details. Delete or mark not applicable any section for a specialty license the facility does not hold.
- **Adopt it.** The owner or governing body must formally adopt the manual and record the adoption date and approval in the minutes or other governance records.
- **Keep it current.** Review the manual at least annually and whenever a statute, rule, form or AHCA guidance changes, or after an inspection finding or incident. Record the revision date and who approved each change.
- **Train staff on it.** All staff must be trained on the policies that apply to their duties. This happens at hire and again whenever a policy changes. Keep signed training and acknowledgment records.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### Who should use it

The owner or governing body, the administrator, designated managers and the person in charge during any absence of the administrator should know the whole manual. Direct-care, medication, food service, housekeeping and maintenance staff must know the sections that govern their work.

### How it is organized

Each policy section states the facility's policy and the procedure staff follow. It names the staff position responsible and identifies the records to be kept. Each section also cites the Florida statute or rule that it implements, so staff and surveyors can trace each policy to its source.

**Appendix A** is a crosswalk. It lists every item from the official documents and rule-listed written-policy requirements that the state uses to review this manual. For each item it names the policy or procedure that satisfies it. Use Appendix A to confirm that nothing required is missing and to find the right policy quickly during a survey.

### Steps for implementation

1. **Customize.** Replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other bracketed placeholders. Confirm the facility's licensed capacity, license type(s) and the specialty services it offers.
2. **Adopt.** Have the governing body adopt the manual and record the date.
3. **Place it where staff can reach it.** Keep a current copy at the facility's physical address, where it can be produced immediately on request. Make it available to residents and their representatives where the rules require it. Rule 59A-36.015 requires records, including required policies, to be readily available at the licensee's physical address.
4. **Train.** Train all staff on the manual at hire and when it changes. Keep signed acknowledgments in personnel records.
5. **Review and update.** Review at least annually and after any change in law, rule, form or practice. Date each revision and keep the superseded version according to the facility's records policy.
6. **Use it in daily practice.** Where a situation is not covered, or the policy is unclear, the administrator decides and then updates the manual.

### Conventions

- Statute and rule citations appear in the exact form used in Florida law, for example "Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C." and "s. 429.26, F.S.".
- Where the manual refers to a state form (for example AHCA Form 3180-5006, AHCA Form 1823, DH Form 1896 or AHCA Form 3180-1006), use the current version published by the issuing agency.
- Dollar amounts, wage figures and rate figures in the manual are reference values. Confirm them against the current official source before relying on them.

### Regulators and contacts

| **AHCA Division of Medicaid, Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) Long-Term Care** | Administers the LTC program that covers assisted living and contracts with LTC plans | 1-877-711-3662 (choice counseling); https://ahca.myflorida.com/medicaid/statewide-medicaid-managed-care/long-term-care-program.html |

| **County health departments (Florida Department of Health)** | Inspect food hygiene, sanitation and biomedical waste (Rule 59A-36.005, F.A.C.) | Contact the local county health department **[COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENT, PHONE]** |
| **Local fire authority / State Fire Marshal** | Inspect fire safety under the Uniform Fire Safety Standards (Rule 59A-36.005, F.A.C.) | **[LOCAL FIRE AUTHORITY, PHONE]** |
| **County emergency management agency** | Final authority on the facility's comprehensive emergency management plan (Rule 59A-36.019, F.A.C.) | **[COUNTY EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AGENCY, PHONE]** |
| **AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse** | Shares Level 2 screening results (s. 435.12, F.S.) | Help line 850-412-4503 (per fact-checked research; confirm before use) |

Under Rule 59A-36.005, F.A.C., the county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste. The local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety. AHCA inspects everything else.

### Official policy checklist and application documents used to review this manual

**Florida does not publish a single policy-and-procedure checklist for ALF licensure.** The AHCA ALF program page lists no such checklist. The license application is filed through the AHCA online licensing system, and renewals are filed online. This manual is therefore organized around the official documents and rule provisions that require written content:

1. **AHCA Form 3180-5006, "Minimum Emergency Management Planning Criteria for Assisted Living Facilities" (September 2023).** Rule 59A-36.019(1), F.A.C. requires the comprehensive emergency management plan (CEMP) to be written on this form. The county emergency management agency is the final administrative authority, and a significant modification must be submitted within 30 days.
2. **Rule 59A-36.019, F.A.C., Emergency Management** (amended eff. 11/23/2023). It lists what the written CEMP must address.
3. **Rule 59A-36.025, F.A.C., Emergency Environmental Control** (amended eff. 11/23/2023). It requires an emergency power plan and written policies and procedures. A new ALF must submit and implement the plan before it obtains a license. After county approval, send proof to AHCA at assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com within 30 days, with a consumer-friendly summary. AHCA offers an Emergency Power Plan Sample Format. The written power policies under subsection (5) must be kept at the facility, producible immediately, and open to residents and their representatives.
4. **Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a), F.A.C., Admission Procedures** (amended eff. 6/11/2025). It lists the written admission-package statement that must be made available to prospective residents. A resident contract or brochure that contains all the listed items satisfies it. Resident contracts must also meet Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C.
5. **Rule 59A-36.021, F.A.C., Extended Congregate Care Services** (amended eff. 9/28/2022). It lists the written policies and procedures an ECC-licensed facility must develop and implement. They apply only if the facility holds or seeks an ECC license, and under subsection (8)(d) they must be kept as a record.
6. **Rule 59A-36.008, F.A.C., Medication Practices** (amended eff. 6/11/2025). It refers to two facility policies: infection control (subsection (3)(h)) and central storage of medication (subsection (6)(b)6.).
7. **Rules 59A-36.020 (Limited Mental Health) and 59A-36.022 (Limited Nursing Services), F.A.C.** These list no written policy topics. They set staffing, records and per-resident plans, so this manual cross-references them rather than taking policy items from them.
8. **Written-policy requirements in the other rules and statutes listed above**, including Rules 59A-36.007, 59A-36.009, 59A-36.010, 59A-36.011, 59A-36.012 and 59A-36.013 and s. 429.28, F.S. Verify each against the current rule text when customizing the manual.

**Appendix A maps every official item to the policy that satisfies it.** For each item in the documents above, Appendix A names the section of this manual that meets it. Use it to confirm completeness before adoption and during any survey.

### Keeping the manual compliant

- **Customize** the manual by replacing all **[AGENCY NAME]** and other bracketed placeholders and by removing sections for specialty licenses the facility does not hold.
- **Adopt** the manual through the owner or governing body and record the date.
- **Keep it current.** Review it at least annually and whenever a statute, rule, form or AHCA guidance changes. Confirm all dollar and wage figures against current official sources.
- **Train staff.** All staff must be trained on the policies relevant to their duties, at hire and when policies change. Keep signed acknowledgments.

citations.title: License Requirements
citations.requirement: Facility may not represent any service beyond its license (1). Capacity changes need prior AHCA Central Office approval (2). Converting uninspected space to resident use needs prior Field Office approval (3). Buildings under one license must be on contiguous property (4). Copies of annual fire and sanitation inspections go to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days (5). Facility must identify state-funded residents on request (6).

citations.title: Admission Procedures, Appropriateness of Placement and Continued Residency Criteria
citations.requirement: (1) Admission criteria, including age 18+, no stage 3-4 pressure sores, not bedridden except hospice, and the listed nursing services that exclude a resident. (2) Face-to-face medical exam within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, on AHCA Form 1823 or the practitioner's form. (3) Admission package contents, and what the resident receives at or before admission. (4) Continued residency: exam at least every 3 years or after a significant change, bedridden limit of 7 consecutive days, stage 2 sore conditions, and terminally ill/hospice retention.

citations.title: Resident Care Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Supervision and written record of significant changes. (2) Activities program (12 hrs/week, 6 days/week). (3) Arrangement for health care and transportation. (5) Bill of Rights posting, written grievance procedure, posted complaint numbers in 14-point type, house rules, no uncompensated work, telephone access. (6) Third-party services and 30-day communication. (7) Elopement standards. (8) Physical restraint care plan. (9) Assistive devices. (10) Infection control: hand hygiene, standard precautions, equipment disinfection.

citations.title: Medication Practices
citations.requirement: Rules for self-administration, pill organizers, assistance with self-administration by trained unlicensed staff, and administration by licensed staff. Also CLIA certificate when facility staff perform lab tests, medication observation records, storage (locked, central storage triggers), disposal timelines, labeling and orders, and OTC/stock supply.

citations.title: Do Not Resuscitate Orders (DNROs)
citations.requirement: Written DNRO policies. A DNRO may not be required as a condition of admission. At admission, give Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent) and DH Form 1896. Document in the record whether DH Form 1896 is executed. Honor an executed form. Hospice procedures take precedence in an arrest.

citations.title: Staffing Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Administrator qualifications (21+, HS/GED, Level 2 screening, core training and competency test within 90 days), up to 3 facilities, managers appointed in writing, and notice of administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006. (2) Staff health statement within 30 days, annual TB documentation, Level 2 for staff and contracted staff, written contracts with staffing agencies. (3) Minimum weekly staff-hours table, awake overnight staff at 17+ residents, CPR/First Aid staff at all times, in-charge rules during administrator absence, written 24-hour schedule, AHCA authority to order more staff.

citations.title: Staff Training Requirements and Competency Test
citations.requirement: 26-hr core training plus competency test (75% to pass) within 3 months; 12 hrs CE every 2 years. 2-hr preservice orientation before resident contact. In-service training: infection control, adverse incidents and emergency procedures, resident rights and abuse, behavior and ADLs, safe food handling, elopement, HIV/AIDS. First Aid/CPR. 6-hr medication-assistance course with 2 hrs annual CE. Food service CE. ECC, LMH and ADRD training.

citations.title: Food Service Standards
citations.requirement: Written food service designee. USDA Dietary Guidelines-based menus, reviewed annually by a dietitian or nutritionist. Menus planned 1 week ahead, and menus as served kept 6 months. Therapeutic diets as ordered. Meal-interval limits. 3-day nonperishable food supply. County health department reports kept for 2 years. Contracted food service documentation.

citations.title: Fiscal Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: resident trust funds not co-mingled with facility funds (a single trust account is allowed with separate written accounting per resident) (2). Surety bond if the facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney (3). Liability insurance in force at all times, with proof filed at each renewal or policy change (4).

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: Records must be readily available at the licensee's physical address. Lists required facility records, including the admission/discharge log, required policies, inspection reports, and the license on display. Also required staff records, resident records, retention (resident contracts 5 years; other resident records 2 years after departure), and inspection access.

citations.title: Resident Contracts
citations.requirement: Contract offered before or at admission with required provisions: services and rates, 30-day written notice of rate increases, deposits and refund policy, written bed hold policy, religious affiliation, transfer notice, 3-year assessment, medication and DNRO policies. Resident gets a copy. Additional charges need an itemized statement and a signed, dated addendum.

citations.title: Emergency Management
citations.requirement: Written CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023) covering the listed components. Annual submission and county emergency management approval, with significant modifications submitted within 30 days. Staff trained within 30 days of hire. Evacuation reporting within 6 hours. Emergency shelter above licensed capacity with a 48-hour report and a log.

citations.title: Emergency Environmental Control for Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Plan to hold ambient temperature at or below 81°F for 96 hours after power loss. At least 20 net sq ft per resident, calculated on 80% of licensed beds. Fuel onsite: 48 hrs (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hrs (17+). Carbon monoxide alarm. Plan submitted before licensure. Proof of county approval sent to AHCA within 30 days. Written heat-injury mitigation procedures. Notice to residents within 5 business days.

citations.title: Inspection Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste (1). Local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety (2). AHCA inspects everything else (3).

citations.title: Physical Plant Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40 fire standards (1)-(2). Resident furnishings (3): bed with mattress at least 36x72 inches, closet or wardrobe, dresser, nightstand or table, lamp, wastebasket. Facility keeps master keys, and provides linens and laundry service.

citations.title: Limited Mental Health
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LMH facility requirements, including a community living support plan and cooperative agreement per mental health resident. Records requirements cross-referenced in 59A-36.015(3)(r). Staffing cross-referenced in 59A-36.010(3)(f).

citations.title: Extended Congregate Care Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: ECC license requirements, including a nurse on staff or under contract, monthly nursing assessments, quarterly service plan review, adequate awake staff at all hours, and ECC admission/residency criteria and disclosure.

citations.title: Limited Nursing Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LNS facility must employ or contract a nurse available as needed. Services require a practitioner's order. Monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes are kept.

citations.title: Licensing and Change of Ownership
citations.requirement: Licensure application and change-of-ownership procedures (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: License required; fee
citations.requirement: A license is required to operate an ALF (subsec. 1). Specialty licenses ECC and LNS (subsec. 3). Biennial fees (subsec. 4).

citations.title: Limited mental health license
citations.requirement: LMH license requirements and training for facilities serving mental health residents.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: Resident contract content and refund policy; implemented by Rule 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents
citations.requirement: Medical examination within 60 days before or 30 days after admission (subsec. 5). Hospice exceptions (subsec. 1). Disagreement on placement appropriateness (subsec. 8), as referenced in Rules 59A-36.006 and 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Use of personnel; emergency care
citations.requirement: Facilities with 17 or more beds must keep a working AED on the premises (subsec. 3(a)). The section also underpins the DNRO rule.

citations.title: Property and personal affairs of residents
citations.requirement: Surety bond when acting as representative payee or under a power of attorney (subsec. 2). Safekeeping of up to $500 cash and $500 in personal effects by mutual consent, and verified statements at least every 3 months (subsecs. 3-4), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Business practice; personnel records; liability insurance
citations.requirement: Records, personnel records and liability insurance (subsec. 3) requirements, per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Resident bill of rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights, grievance and facility-procedure rights. It is cited in Rules 59A-36.007(5) and 59A-36.011 and in the fact-checked research. Section text was not independently re-fetched in this pass, so confirm subsection details before quoting them.

citations.title: Staff training and educational requirements
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for core training, 12-hour administrator CE (subsec. 5) and the medication-assistance training (subsec. 6).

citations.title: Background screening
citations.requirement: Level 2 background screening of owners, administrators and staff.

citations.title: Background screening; prohibited offenses
citations.requirement: Level 2 screening standards, with rescreening every 5 years (subsec. 2), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are shared through the AHCA Clearinghouse (help line 850-412-4503 per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Long-term care managed care plan accountability
citations.requirement: SMMC LTC plans and ALFs negotiate rates. There is no state rate table.

citations.title: Health care licensing application procedures
citations.requirement: Online licensing and renewal filing. Per fact-checked research, renewals must be filed online (effective 3/5/2024).

citations.title: Florida minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage is $15.00/hr from Sept 30, 2026.

citations.title: Optional State Supplementation
citations.requirement: OSS base provider rate $991.40/month and $160 personal needs allowance (eff. 6/24/2025), per fact-checked research. DCF determines eligibility.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Owner/governing body, administrator, facility managers, persons in charge
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, who is accountable for the Assisted Living Facility (ALF), and the qualifications, training and succession requirements for the administrator, so the facility is always led by a qualified, accountable person.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates under a governing body (the owner or the owner's designated board) that holds final legal responsibility for the facility, adopts its policies, and appoints a qualified administrator. The administrator must be at least 21 years old, hold a high school diploma or GED, pass Level 2 background screening, and complete the 26-hour core training and pass the competency test (75% to pass) within 90 days, as required by Rule 59A-36.010(1) and Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C. The administrator completes 12 hours of continuing education every 2 years (s. 429.52, F.S.; Rule 59A-36.011). One administrator may oversee no more than 3 ALFs, and a manager must be appointed in writing for each facility. AHCA is notified of any administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006. A person in charge is designated in writing for every period when the administrator is absent. The facility operates only within the license issued under s. 429.07, F.S. No item on the state checklist is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: The owner, or the board or members the owner designates, with final legal authority over the facility.
The person who meets Rule 59A-36.010(1) qualifications and is responsible for daily operation and compliance.
A person appointed in writing to manage a facility when one administrator oversees more than one ALF.
The staff member designated in writing to be responsible for the facility when the administrator is not on site.
The 26-hour state-approved core curriculum with a competency test (75% to pass).

procedures: The governing body adopts a written organizational chart and a written statement of its responsibilities at the time of licensure and reviews both annually.

The governing body appoints the administrator in writing. Before the start date, the HR designee verifies age 21 or older, a high school diploma or GED, and a passed Level 2 screening, and files copies in the personnel record.

The administrator completes the 26-hour core training and passes the competency test (75%) within 90 days of becoming administrator. The governing body keeps the certificate and test result in the personnel file.

The administrator completes 12 hours of continuing education every 2 years. The HR designee tracks the due date on a training calendar and alerts the administrator and the governing body 90 days before the deadline.

If one administrator will oversee more than one facility, the governing body confirms that the total does not exceed 3 ALFs and appoints a manager for each facility in writing, with a copy kept on site and in the personnel record.
The governing body states in writing the duties delegated to the administrator, including hiring, scheduling, resident admissions and discharges, budget, and regulatory compliance.

The administrator posts or keeps available, in a location readily accessible on site, the name and the 24-hour contact number of the administrator and the current person in charge: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [PHONE].

Before any planned absence, the administrator designates a person in charge in writing, naming the dates of the absence. The person in charge must meet the staffing and training requirements of Rule 59A-36.010(3), including current CPR and First Aid.
The administrator briefs the person in charge on residents with changes of condition, pending admissions or discharges, and how to reach the administrator and the owner.
The administrator keeps the written designation on site for review by surveyors and records every absence and the person in charge on the shift schedule.
When the administrator changes, the governing body submits AHCA Form 3180-1006 to AHCA within 10 days of the change. The HR designee keeps proof of submission with the facility records.
The administrator reports to the governing body at least quarterly on census, staffing, incidents, grievances, inspections, training compliance and finances. Minutes are kept.
The governing body reviews the administrator's performance annually and documents the review.
The administrator ensures the facility represents only the services allowed under its license (see GOV-02) and that policies are in writing and followed.

If the administrator leaves unexpectedly, the governing body appoints an interim person in charge in writing the same day and begins the process of appointing a qualified administrator and notifying AHCA within 10 days.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt policies, appoint a qualified administrator in writing, review reports quarterly, and ensure resources for compliance.
Meet qualifications and CE, operate the facility day to day, designate a person in charge, and file notices with AHCA.
Manage the assigned facility under written appointment and report to the administrator.
Act for the administrator during designated absences, following the written designation.
Verify qualifications, track training deadlines, and maintain the administrator's personnel file.

documentation: Organizational chart and governing body statement of responsibilities
Administrator personnel file: age and education proof, Level 2 screening result, core training certificate and competency test result, CE certificates
Written manager appointments (if applicable)
Written person-in-charge designations
AHCA Form 3180-1006 and proof of submission
Governing body meeting minutes and administrator performance review

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Policy Review and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, all staff
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] is licensed before it admits residents, operates only within its license, maintains required postings and records, and meets Florida requirements for inspections, capacity changes, renewal and policy review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not admit or serve any resident until AHCA has issued the ALF license (s. 429.07(1), F.S.; Rule 59A-36.003, F.A.C.). The facility will not represent or offer any service beyond its license type (standard, Extended Congregate Care, Limited Nursing Services, or Limited Mental Health) (Rule 59A-36.004(1)). Licensed capacity will not change without prior approval of the AHCA Central Office, and space that has not been inspected will not be converted to resident use without prior AHCA Field Office approval (Rule 59A-36.004(2)-(3)). Buildings under one license must be on contiguous property (Rule 59A-36.004(4)). Copies of the annual fire and sanitation inspections are sent to the AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days (Rule 59A-36.004(5)). The license is displayed, renewals are filed online (Rule 59A-35.060), records are readily available at the facility address (Rule 59A-36.015), and written policies are reviewed at least annually with a dated revision log. No item on the state checklist is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: The Florida Agency for Health Care Administration, which licenses and surveys ALFs.
An Extended Congregate Care (ECC), Limited Nursing Services (LNS) or Limited Mental Health (LMH) license that allows services beyond the standard license.
The number of residents the facility is licensed to serve, as shown on the license.
A dated record of each policy review, who performed it, and what changed.

procedures: Before opening, the owner submits the licensure application and fees to AHCA as required by Rule 59A-36.003 and Rule 59A-35.060. The administrator keeps a copy of the application and receipt.

The facility admits no resident, accepts no deposit for a bed, and begins no care until the ALF license is issued. The administrator confirms the license in hand and records the effective date in the admission/discharge log file.
The administrator displays the current license in a conspicuous public place at the facility and keeps a copy in the administrative file.

The administrator compares the license to the services offered. Marketing materials, the admission agreement and care practice must not mention or provide any service that exceeds the license (standard, ECC, LNS, LMH). The administrator reviews all marketing before it is released.
If the facility wants a specialty license, the owner applies to AHCA and does not provide the specialty services until the license is issued.
The owner does not increase or decrease licensed capacity without prior written approval from the AHCA Central Office. The administrator keeps the approval letter.
Before using any room, wing or building not previously inspected for resident use, the administrator requests and obtains approval from the AHCA Field Office, and records the date.
If the facility operates more than one building under the license, the administrator confirms the buildings are on contiguous property and keeps the site plan on file.

The administrator schedules the county health department inspection (sanitation, food hygiene, biomedical waste) and the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspection, as described in Rule 59A-36.005. AHCA inspects all other areas.
Within 30 calendar days after each annual fire and sanitation inspection, the administrator sends copies to the AHCA Central Office and keeps proof of sending.

During any survey, the administrator or person in charge accompanies the surveyor, provides access to all areas and records, and keeps copies of items provided. Records are kept at the facility address as required by Rule 59A-36.015.
The administrator tracks the license expiration date on a compliance calendar. Renewal is filed online, with the fee, before the deadline, and the confirmation is kept.
Within 30 days after the receipt of an inspection report or survey, the administrator prepares any required plan of correction and reports results to the governing body (see GOV-03).

The administrator reviews every policy in this manual at least annually, and whenever a rule, statute or AHCA instruction changes. Each review is entered in the revision log with date, reviewer and changes made. Staff are trained on any change before it takes effect.
A copy of the written policies is kept at the facility and available for AHCA inspection, with the current inspection reports and license, as listed in Rule 59A-36.015.
The governing body is told of any change of ownership; a change of ownership requires a new licensure process under Rule 59A-36.003 and is not carried out until AHCA approves.

responsibilities.duty: File applications and renewals, approve capacity decisions, and ensure no admission before licensure.
Display the license, keep services within the license type, submit inspection copies, manage the compliance calendar and policy reviews.
Support surveyors and make records available when the administrator is absent.
Describe only services the license allows.

documentation: Current license and licensure application/renewal confirmations
AHCA approval letters for capacity or space changes
Fire and sanitation inspection reports and proof of sending to AHCA Central Office
Compliance calendar
Policy revision log with dated reviews
Survey reports, plans of correction and correspondence with AHCA
Admission/discharge log

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Risk Management and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, department leads, all staff
policies.purpose: To provide an ongoing program that finds, tracks and corrects risks and quality problems affecting residents, and to make sure the governing body regularly reviews the results.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an internal quality assurance and risk management program, including adverse incident tracking, under Florida's ALF risk management requirements. The administrator reviews incidents, grievances, falls, medication errors and elopements and presents them to the governing body at least quarterly. Survey deficiencies and plans of correction are tracked until corrected. Staff are trained on adverse incidents and emergency procedures within 30 days of hire (Rule 59A-36.011), and supervise and record significant changes in residents (Rule 59A-36.007(1)). Before publication of this manual, the administrator must confirm current statutory timelines for adverse incident reporting; this policy does not state a reporting deadline other than those set out in SAF-02 and REC-02. No item on the state checklist is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: An event over which the facility could exercise control that results in serious harm or risk to a resident, as defined in Florida law and reported under SAF-02 and REC-02.
A routine review of data and practice to identify and correct problems.
A written plan submitted to AHCA that states how and when a survey deficiency will be corrected.
A repeated pattern of events by type, location, time, staff or resident.

procedures: The governing body designates the administrator as QA/risk manager in writing and may name a committee that includes the administrator, the nurse or health care designee, a direct care staff member and the dietary lead.

Staff record every incident, fall, medication error, elopement or attempt, resident injury, grievance and significant change of condition on the facility's incident or log forms the same shift (see SAF-02, HS-04).

The administrator reviews each report within one business day, makes sure the resident is safe and the family, physician or representative is notified as required, and decides whether state reporting is required (see REC-02).
The administrator keeps a running QA log that records, by month, the number and type of incidents, falls, medication errors, elopements, grievances, hospital transfers and infection events.

At least quarterly, the QA committee reviews the log for trends by resident, time of day, location, staffing and type, and writes up actions. The review is presented to the governing body and minuted.
For each trend or high-risk event, the committee assigns an action, a responsible person and a due date (for example, retraining, equipment repair, care plan change, change of staffing).
The administrator follows up on each action by the due date and records whether the problem has been corrected, using the next quarter's data to check.
The administrator logs every AHCA survey, complaint investigation and inspection finding with the date, the deficiency and the plan of correction, and tracks completion until AHCA accepts correction.
The administrator verifies each new employee completes training on adverse incidents and emergency procedures within 30 days of hire, and records the date on the training record (see STF-03).
The administrator reviews resident care records at least quarterly on a sample basis for documentation of significant changes, service plan updates and physician notification.
The administrator reviews the medication error log with the person responsible for medication oversight (see HS-01, HS-02) and obtains retraining for any staff member involved in an error.
The QA process includes an annual review of resident and family feedback, including grievances and any satisfaction surveys, and the results are recorded.
The administrator treats all QA data as confidential and does not use it to retaliate against staff or residents who report concerns in good faith.
The annual QA summary, including goals for the coming year, is signed by the administrator and filed with the governing body minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Review QA results at least quarterly and provide resources for corrective actions.
Maintain the QA log, review incidents, track plans of correction and report to the governing body.
Complete assigned actions by the due date and report results.
Report incidents and near misses promptly and complete assigned training.

documentation: Incident, fall, medication error and elopement reports
QA log and quarterly trend reviews
Governing body minutes with QA review
Survey reports and plan of correction tracker
Training records for adverse incident and emergency procedures
Annual QA summary

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, billing and admissions staff, all employees
federal: 31 USC 3729 (False Claims Act, if billing Medicaid)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills and collects only what is owed, deals honestly with residents, payers and regulators, and prevents and reports fraud, waste and abuse.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] charges only for services listed in the resident's admission agreement or a signed written addendum. When the facility serves Medicaid residents through Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) Long-Term Care plans, rates are negotiated between the plan and the facility under s. 409.982, F.S.; there is no state rate table, and the facility will bill only the negotiated rate for services actually delivered. For residents who receive Optional State Supplementation (OSS), the facility respects the OSS base provider rate ($991.40 per month) and the $160 personal needs allowance effective 6/24/2025 (s. 409.212 and Rule 65A-2.036, F.A.C.). The Department of Children and Families (DCF) determines eligibility. Third-party supplementation is voluntary and is never a condition of admission or stay. The facility identifies state-funded residents to AHCA on request (Rule 59A-36.004(6)). If the facility bills Medicaid, it complies with the federal False Claims Act (31 USC 3729) and the Anti-Kickback Statute (42 USC 1320a-7b(b)). No item on the state checklist is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: A request for payment that the facility knows or should know is false, including billing for services not delivered.
Offering, paying, soliciting or receiving anything of value to induce or reward referrals of Medicaid-covered business.
Optional State Supplementation, a state cash supplement for eligible ALF residents; DCF determines eligibility.
A voluntary payment by a family member or other person, beyond the OSS rate, which may not be required as a condition of admission.
A managed care plan that contracts with the state to cover long-term care services, including assisted living, for eligible Medicaid enrollees.

procedures: The governing body appoints the administrator, or another named person, as compliance officer and records the appointment in the minutes.
Each employee receives a copy of this policy at hire, and the HR designee documents the receipt and training during orientation. Training is repeated annually.
Admissions staff prepare the admission agreement so that every rate, fee and service is listed (see RR-03). No charge is made unless it appears in the agreement or a signed addendum.
Before adding or changing a charge, the administrator prepares a written addendum, reviews it with the resident or representative, gives the resident a copy and obtains a signature.

For SMMC LTC plan residents, the billing designee confirms the negotiated rate in the written plan contract, bills only for dates the resident was present and receiving care, and does not bill the resident for amounts the plan covers.

For OSS residents, the billing designee confirms with DCF eligibility records and does not charge more than the OSS base provider rate for room and board, and does not take any portion of the $160 personal needs allowance as payment for services (see RR-04).

If a family member offers third-party supplementation, the administrator documents in writing that the payment is voluntary, the amount, and what it covers. Admission and continued stay are never conditioned on supplementation.
On request from AHCA, the administrator identifies the state-funded residents (Rule 59A-36.004(6)) within the time AHCA specifies and keeps a copy of the response.

The billing designee reconciles billing to the daily census and the admission/discharge log every month and corrects any error found by refunding or crediting the overpayment within 30 days of discovery.

No employee may offer, pay, solicit or accept money, gifts or any item of value in return for referring residents or for arranging services paid for by Medicaid. Any offer must be reported to the compliance officer the same day.

Employees may report concerns about billing or compliance to the compliance officer, the administrator or the governing body, in person or in writing, including anonymously at [PHONE]. Staff who report in good faith will not be retaliated against.
The compliance officer investigates each report within 10 business days, documents findings and corrective action, and informs the governing body at the next quarterly review (see GOV-03).
If an overpayment or suspected fraud is found, the compliance officer consults the facility's legal counsel and reports as required to the payer or the appropriate authority.
The facility screens new hires and contractors against the registries described in STF-02 so that excluded persons are not employed or paid.
The compliance officer reviews this policy annually and keeps records of training, reports and investigations for at least 5 years.

responsibilities.duty: Appoint the compliance officer, set a culture of honest billing, and review compliance reports.
Train staff, investigate reports, audit billing and correct errors.
Bill accurately under the contract, reconcile to the census and refund overpayments.
Follow this policy, never accept kickbacks and report concerns.

documentation: Compliance officer appointment
Employee acknowledgment and training records
Signed admission agreements and addenda
Monthly billing reconciliation
Payer contracts and negotiated-rate records
Voluntary third-party supplementation statements
Compliance reports, investigations and corrective actions
Responses to AHCA requests regarding state-funded residents

policies.title: Liability Insurance, Workers' Compensation and Fiscal Standards
policies.applies_to: Owner, administrator, business office staff
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] maintains required insurance, pays lawful wages, protects resident funds, and keeps fiscal practices that meet Florida ALF requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps liability insurance in force at all times and files proof with AHCA at each renewal or policy change (Rule 59A-36.013(4); s. 429.275(3), F.S.). Rule does not set a dollar minimum; the governing body sets limits after consulting its insurer. The certificate states the facility name, street address, ALF status, licensed capacity and policy dates. Workers' compensation coverage is carried when the facility has four or more employees (Ch. 440, F.S.). All employees are paid at or above the Florida minimum wage under Art. X, s. 24, Fla. Const. ($14.00 per hour from 9/30/2025 and $15.00 per hour from 9/30/2026). Resident trust funds are never co-mingled with facility funds; a single trust account is permitted only with a separate written accounting for each resident (Rule 59A-36.013(2)). If the facility is a resident's representative payee or acts under a power of attorney, it obtains a surety bond (Rule 59A-36.013(3); s. 429.27(2), F.S.). No item on the state checklist is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: A document from the insurer showing the coverage, insured, location, limits and policy period.
Money belonging to residents that the facility holds for them, kept apart from facility money.
A bond protecting a resident's funds when the facility acts as representative payee or under a power of attorney.
A person or organization appointed to receive and manage a beneficiary's government benefits.

procedures: Before the license is issued, the owner obtains general and professional liability insurance for the facility at the address and licensed capacity, and confirms there is no gap in coverage.

The administrator reviews the certificate of insurance and verifies it shows the facility name, street address, that it is an ALF, licensed capacity, and the policy start and end dates. Errors are corrected by the insurer before filing.
The administrator files proof of coverage with AHCA at each license renewal and whenever the policy is changed or replaced, and keeps the filing confirmation.

The administrator records the policy expiration date on the compliance calendar and begins renewal at least 60 days in advance so coverage never lapses. If coverage would lapse, the administrator notifies the owner immediately.

The owner obtains workers' compensation coverage as soon as the facility has four or more employees and keeps the policy and proof of coverage on file. The facility posts any required workers' compensation notice.
The business office confirms that every employee's pay rate is at or above the applicable Florida minimum wage and updates all pay rates before September 30, 2026, to at least $15.00 per hour.
Payroll records show hours worked and pay for each employee. Overtime is calculated under applicable wage law.

The facility keeps all resident money in an account separate from facility operating funds. If a single trust account is used, the business office keeps a separate written ledger for each resident (see RR-04).
Facility money is never deposited into the trust account, and resident money is never used to pay facility expenses.
If the facility will be a representative payee or act under a power of attorney for a resident, the owner obtains the surety bond before taking over any funds and keeps a copy of the bond.
The administrator provides each resident with a verified written statement of any funds held at least every 3 months (s. 429.27) and keeps a signed copy.
The business office prepares an annual operating budget approved by the governing body, including reserves for maintenance and emergencies.
The owner has the books reviewed at least annually, and the administrator corrects any finding and reports it to the governing body.
All fiscal records are retained at the facility or readily available there (see REC-01).

responsibilities.duty: Purchase and maintain insurance and the surety bond, approve the budget and review financial reports.
Verify certificates, file proof with AHCA, track expiration dates and ensure resident funds are protected.
Run payroll to wage law, maintain separate resident ledgers and prepare quarterly statements.

documentation: Certificate of liability insurance and AHCA filing confirmations
Workers' compensation policy
Payroll records and wage rate schedule
Resident trust account records and individual ledgers
Quarterly resident fund statements with signatures
Surety bond (if applicable)
Annual budget and financial review

policies.title: Resident Rights, Bill of Rights and House Rules
policies.applies_to: All residents, representatives, and all staff
policies.purpose: To protect each resident's legal rights, make sure residents and families know them, and make sure the facility's house rules are given in writing before admission and do not conflict with those rights.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] posts the Resident Bill of Rights (s. 429.28, F.S.; Rule 59A-36.007(5), F.A.C.), explains it to residents and representatives, and follows it. This policy meets Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a)10., F.A.C. (facility rules and regulations that residents must follow, as described in Rule 59A-36.007). The facility gives each resident or representative a written copy of the house rules at or before admission as part of the admission package (Rule 59A-36.006(3)). House rules must not limit rights guaranteed by the Bill of Rights. Residents are not required to perform work for the facility without compensation, and telephone access is preserved (Rule 59A-36.007(5)). No resident is retaliated against for exercising rights or for making a complaint. For Medicaid residents, the facility also follows the home and community-based settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4). Staff must confirm the exact subsection wording of s. 429.28 with current law before quoting it to residents.

definitions.definition: The statement of rights for ALF residents under s. 429.28, F.S., that the facility must post and honor.
The written facility rules and regulations that residents must follow, as described in Rule 59A-36.007.
A person legally authorized to act for the resident, such as a health care surrogate, guardian or agent under power of attorney.
Any adverse action against a resident because the resident asserted a right, complained or contacted an outside agency.

procedures: The administrator posts the current Resident Bill of Rights in a conspicuous place that residents and visitors can read, in 14-point type or larger for the posted complaint numbers (see RR-02), and checks monthly that the posting is intact.

The administrator drafts the written house rules covering matters such as visiting hours, meals, quiet hours, smoking (see SAF-14), guests, pets, personal property, use of common areas and safety. Rules must be reasonable and must not conflict with the Bill of Rights or the licensure rules.
The governing body approves the house rules. The administrator reviews them at least annually and whenever a rule changes, and records the review in the policy revision log (GOV-02).

Before or at admission, the admissions designee gives the resident and representative a copy of the Bill of Rights and the house rules in the admission package (ADM-02). This meets Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a)10.
The admissions designee reviews the Bill of Rights and house rules with the resident and representative, in a language and manner they understand (see RR-07), and answers questions.
The resident or representative signs an acknowledgment of receipt of both documents. A copy is given to the resident and the original is placed in the resident record.
When a house rule changes, the administrator gives each resident and representative written notice before the change takes effect and keeps a signed or dated record of delivery.
Staff treat residents with courtesy, dignity and respect, honoring privacy, choice of schedule, religious practice, visitors and the right to manage personal affairs as the Bill of Rights allows.

The facility does not require residents to do work for the facility. A resident may volunteer for a task only if it is therapeutic, listed in the service plan, and either compensated or truly voluntary, and the resident may stop at any time.

Residents may use a telephone privately at any reasonable time. The administrator keeps a working telephone available in a private place and does not restrict outgoing or incoming calls except as the resident or the law allows.
Residents may contact the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, AHCA, the Abuse Hotline and their lawyer without interference (see RR-02 and SAF-01).

No staff member may retaliate against a resident or family member for exercising a right or filing a complaint. A suspected incident of retaliation is reported to the administrator the same day, investigated within 3 business days and documented.

For residents who receive Medicaid, the administrator reviews facility practices against the HCBS settings requirements at 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4), including privacy, choice and visitors, and documents any modification and its reason in the person-centered service plan.
All employees receive training on the Bill of Rights and resident rights at orientation and at least annually (Rule 59A-36.011; see STF-03).
The administrator reviews resident complaints and rights concerns quarterly with the QA process (GOV-03) and corrects any pattern.

responsibilities.duty: Approve house rules and ensure they do not conflict with resident rights.
Post the Bill of Rights, maintain the house rules, review annually and investigate any alleged rights violation or retaliation.
Provide and explain the Bill of Rights and house rules before admission and obtain the signed acknowledgment.
Honor each resident's rights and report violations or retaliation.

documentation: Posted Resident Bill of Rights
Written house rules and revision log
Signed acknowledgment of receipt of Bill of Rights and house rules in the resident record
Notices of house rule changes with delivery records
Records of rights complaints, investigations and outcomes
Staff training records on resident rights

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
policies.applies_to: All staff, residents, residents' representatives, and visitors at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident can raise a concern or complaint freely and without fear of retaliation, and that each concern is investigated, answered, and documented. To keep residents' access to outside complaint agencies and to the Long-Term Care Ombudsman open at all times.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written grievance procedure that is given to each resident (and representative, if any) at or before admission and is available to any resident at any time, as required by Rule 59A-36.007(5), F.A.C. Residents may complain about any aspect of care, services, staff, other residents, or house rules, and may complain to the facility or to an outside agency, or both. The facility does not discourage outside complaints and does not retaliate against any resident, representative, family member, or employee for making a complaint. This is consistent with the Resident Bill of Rights in s. 429.28, F.S. The facility posts the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873), the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) Assisted Living Unit contact information, and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program contact information in a conspicuous location accessible to residents and visitors, printed in at least 14-point type. Ombudsman representatives and authorized agency representatives are given access to residents and may speak with any resident privately.

definitions.definition: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction or concern by or for a resident about care, services, treatment, staff conduct, rights, charges, or the facility environment.
A representative of the Florida Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, who advocates for residents of long-term care facilities and may receive and help resolve complaints.
Any adverse action, threat, discrimination, or discouragement directed at a person because the person made or supported a complaint.
The unit of the Agency for Health Care Administration, Bureau of Health Facility Regulation, that licenses and surveys assisted living facilities: (850) 412-4304; assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com.

procedures: The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) maintains the written grievance procedure and reviews it at least annually with the policy review required by GOV-02.

At or before admission, the admissions staff member gives the resident (and representative) a copy of the grievance procedure, explains it in plain language (using interpreter or translated materials if needed, see RR-07), and records delivery on the admission checklist (ADM-02).

The Administrator posts, in a common area readily visible to residents and visitors, a notice listing the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873), the AHCA Assisted Living Unit ((850) 412-4304; assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com), and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program ([OMBUDSMAN PROGRAM TOLL-FREE NUMBER]). The notice is printed in at least 14-point type.

The Administrator checks the posted numbers and email address against the current AHCA and Ombudsman Program contact information at least once each year and whenever the facility is notified of a change. Outdated notices are replaced the same day.

Any staff member who receives a complaint, oral or written, listens, does not argue or discourage the resident, and records it on the Grievance Log/Form the same shift. If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect, or exploitation, the staff member also follows SAF-01 immediately and reports to the Abuse Hotline.
Staff give a resident who wants to file a written complaint a grievance form and offer help writing it. A resident may also use a trusted person, a representative, or the Ombudsman for help.
The Administrator (or designee not involved in the complaint) acknowledges every grievance to the resident within 2 business days. This is a facility standard.

The Administrator investigates promptly: interviews the resident, any witnesses, and involved staff; reviews the resident record and service plan; and writes findings. The investigation is started within 2 business days of receipt.

The Administrator gives the resident (and representative, if authorized) a written response within 10 business days, stating findings, any action taken, and how to take the concern further. If more time is needed, the resident is told why and given a date for the answer.
The written response always tells the resident that he or she may contact the Ombudsman, AHCA, or the Abuse Hotline at any time, whether or not the facility has resolved the matter.
Staff must not interfere with a resident's private telephone, mail, or email communication with the Ombudsman, AHCA, or any other outside agency (see RR-06).

When an Ombudsman representative or an AHCA or other authorized agency representative arrives, staff verify identification, notify the Administrator or person in charge, and give access to residents and to records as the law allows. Staff do not delay entry or screen who may speak with residents. Residents may decline a visit.
The Administrator reviews the grievance log monthly, identifies trends or repeat issues (by staff member, shift, or service), and reports them to the quality assurance process (GOV-03).
If a resident or employee reports retaliation, the Administrator investigates it as a separate grievance and takes corrective action, including discipline up to termination for staff.
The Administrator trains all new staff on this policy at orientation and trains all staff annually (STF-03).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the procedure, posts the notice, investigates and answers grievances, trends the log, and protects against retaliation.
Accept complaints without discouraging them, record them the same shift, report abuse allegations immediately, and never retaliate.
Give the grievance procedure at or before admission and document delivery.
Reviews grievance trends and monitors corrective action (GOV-03).

documentation: Written grievance procedure and signed receipt in the resident record
Grievance Log/Form: date received, complainant, nature of concern, investigator, findings, action, response date
Written response to the resident
Photo or copy of posted complaint notice with date of last verification
Ombudsman and agency visit log
Training sign-in sheets

policies.title: Admission Agreement (Resident Contract), Fees, Deposits and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Administrator, admissions staff, business office staff, residents and their representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident and representative receives a clear written contract before or at admission that states what [AGENCY NAME] provides, what it costs, and the conditions for deposits, refunds, rate changes, and transfer. To ensure that no charge is made that the resident has not agreed to in writing.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] offers every prospective resident a written contract before or at admission, as required by Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C., and s. 429.24, F.S. The resident receives a copy. The contract is also part of the admission package under Rule 59A-36.006(3), F.A.C. This policy meets the following official items of Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a), F.A.C.: item 2 (the daily, weekly, or monthly charge and the services, supplies, and accommodations provided for that rate); item 3 (personal care services the facility is prepared to provide and additional costs, if any); item 4 (nursing services the facility is prepared to provide and additional costs, if any); item 6 (availability of transportation and additional costs, if any); item 7 (other special services provided by the facility and additional cost, if any); and item 9 (services the facility does not provide but will arrange for the resident, and additional cost, if any). The contract also states: services and rates; deposits and the refund policy; a written bed hold policy; the facility's religious affiliation, if any; transfer notice requirements; the requirement for a medical and assessment update at least every 3 years or after a significant change; the facility's medication policy; and the facility's Do Not Resuscitate Order (DNRO) policy (RR-05). The contract explains how disagreement about the appropriateness of the placement is addressed under s. 429.26, F.S. The facility gives residents at least 30 days' written notice of any rate increase. Charges beyond the contract rate are made only with an itemized statement and a signed, dated addendum. The contract is retained for 5 years (REC-01).

definitions.definition: The written agreement between the facility and the resident (or representative) setting out services, rates, and conditions of residency.
A signed and dated written amendment to the contract that adds a service or charge, supported by an itemized statement.
Reservation of a resident's bed during a temporary absence (e.g., hospital stay), governed by the facility's written bed hold policy in the contract.
Money paid in advance of or at admission that is refundable or applicable under the terms stated in the contract.

procedures: Before the resident moves in, admissions staff review the facility's current rate schedule and the results of the pre-admission screening (ADM-01) and determine which services, if any, carry additional charges.

The Administrator or designee completes the contract so that it states the daily, weekly, or monthly rate and lists the services, supplies, and accommodations included in that rate (Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a)2.).
The contract lists the personal care services the facility is prepared to provide and any additional cost, or states that none applies (item 3).
The contract lists the nursing services the facility is prepared to provide (see HS-03) and any additional cost, or states that none applies (item 4).
The contract states whether transportation is available (see DL-04), which trips are included, and any additional cost, or states that none applies (item 6).
The contract lists other special services provided (such as laundry, beauty/barber, escort, or special activities) and any additional cost (item 7).
The contract lists services the facility does not provide but will arrange (such as home health, therapy, or hospice through outside providers), and any additional cost (item 9).

The contract states each deposit, what it is for, and the refund policy, including the timeframe and conditions for refund of deposits and prepaid amounts: [REFUND TIMEFRAME AND CONDITIONS PER CONTRACT].

The contract includes the written bed hold policy, the religious affiliation statement (or a statement that there is none), the transfer notice requirements (see ADM-06), the 3-year assessment requirement (ADM-03), and the medication policy (HS-01, HS-02) and DNRO policy (RR-05).
The contract states that rate increases require 30 days' written notice to the resident or representative.

Admissions staff review the contract with the resident and representative in plain language, offer an interpreter or translated copy if needed (RR-07), and answer questions. The contract is offered before or at admission, so the resident has the chance to read it before signing.
The resident (or legal representative) and the Administrator or designee sign and date the contract. The resident receives a complete copy; the receipt is documented on the admission checklist.
Business office staff do not accept any deposit or payment that is not stated in the contract. Each payment is receipted in writing.

When a service not covered by the contract is requested or becomes necessary, the Administrator prepares an itemized statement of the service and charge and an addendum. The resident or representative must sign and date it before the charge is applied. The resident receives a copy.
For a rate increase, the business office prepares a written notice, delivers it to the resident or representative at least 30 days before the effective date, and keeps a copy with proof of delivery.
On discharge or transfer, the business office calculates any refund, prepares an itemized accounting, and issues the refund as stated in the contract. Disputes are handled under RR-02.
The Administrator reviews the contract template at least annually and whenever rates or services change, and has counsel review it where the facility so decides.
The signed contract is filed in the resident record and kept for 5 years, in line with REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the contract template and rates, signs contracts, approves addenda and rate-increase notices.
Complete and explain the contract, obtain signatures, give a copy to the resident, and file the original.
Receipt payments, issue addendum-based charges only with signed approval, deliver 30-day rate notices, and compute refunds.
Review and sign the contract and any addendum.

documentation: Signed and dated resident contract with copy-receipt noted on the admission checklist
Current rate and services schedule
Itemized statements and signed addenda
30-day rate-increase notices with proof of delivery
Deposit receipts and refund accountings
Bed hold policy acknowledgment

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: Administrator, business office staff, and all staff who handle resident funds or belongings
policies.purpose: To protect residents' money and personal property from loss, misuse, or exploitation, and to ensure that any funds held by [AGENCY NAME] are kept separate from facility funds, bonded where required, and accounted for in writing.
policies.policy: Residents manage their own funds and property unless they ask otherwise or have a legal representative. [AGENCY NAME] does not require a resident to give it control over money or property. The facility never co-mingles resident funds with facility operating funds. Under Rule 59A-36.013, F.A.C., if resident funds are held in a trust account, they are kept separately from facility funds, and if a single trust account is used, a separate written accounting is kept for each resident. If the facility acts as a resident's representative payee, or holds a power of attorney for a resident, it maintains a surety bond as required by s. 429.27, F.S., and Rule 59A-36.013, F.A.C., and files a copy with AHCA each year. By mutual consent, the facility may safekeep up to $500 in cash and up to $500 in personal effects for a resident. The facility gives each resident for whom it holds funds a verified written statement at least every 3 months, as required by s. 429.27, F.S. Staff do not borrow from, accept gifts from, or benefit financially from residents (STF-06).

definitions.definition: A person or organization appointed by a benefits agency (e.g., Social Security) to receive and manage benefits for a beneficiary.
A legal document authorizing a person to act on another's behalf in financial or other matters.
A bond that guarantees reimbursement for loss of resident funds, required when the facility is a representative payee or holds a power of attorney.
A separate account for resident funds, not commingled with facility operating funds.
Holding resident cash or valuables for the resident at the resident's request, by mutual consent, up to the limits in this policy.

procedures: At admission, admissions staff tell the resident (and representative) that the resident may keep and manage his or her own money and property, and ask whether the resident wants the facility to safekeep any cash or valuables. The answer is recorded.

The facility safekeeps funds or property only by mutual written consent, signed by the resident or legal representative and the Administrator, and never above $500 in cash and $500 in personal effects.

When cash is deposited for safekeeping, two staff members count it with the resident or representative present when possible. The staff member issues a numbered written receipt and a copy goes to the resident.

Safekept cash and valuables are locked in a secure location. Only the Administrator and the designated business office staff member have access. Funds are never kept in a staff member's personal possession.
If the facility accepts resident funds into a trust account, the Administrator opens it as a separate account, labeled as resident funds, apart from all operating accounts.
If a single trust account is used, the business office keeps a separate written ledger for each resident showing each deposit, withdrawal, date, purpose, and balance.

Every withdrawal requires the resident's (or representative's) written or signed authorization and a receipt. The business office does not pay facility charges from resident funds unless the contract or a signed authorization permits it (RR-03).

Before the facility becomes a resident's representative payee or accepts a power of attorney for any resident, the Administrator obtains a surety bond. The Administrator files a copy of the bond with AHCA each year and keeps the current bond in the facility's records.

The business office gives each resident whose funds or valuables the facility holds a verified written statement at least every 3 months. The statement lists the opening balance, all transactions, the closing balance, and the safekept items. The resident or representative signs for receipt.

On discharge, transfer, or death, the business office provides a final accounting within the timeframe stated in the contract ([TIMEFRAME PER CONTRACT]) and returns funds and property to the resident, representative, or legal representative of the estate, obtaining a signed receipt (see HS-08 for death).

Staff keep an inventory of a resident's personal property at admission if the resident or representative requests it, and update it when items are added or removed. The resident or representative signs the inventory.

Staff who learn of lost, missing, or suspected misused funds or property report it to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator investigates, reports suspected exploitation under SAF-01, and notifies the resident or representative.
The Administrator or an independent party reconciles the trust account and resident ledgers monthly and keeps the reconciliation on file. Discrepancies are resolved and documented the same month.
The Administrator reviews bond status, trust account practices, and statements quarterly as part of GOV-05 and GOV-03 reviews.

responsibilities.duty: Approves safekeeping arrangements, maintains the surety bond, files the copy with AHCA yearly, and oversees reconciliation.
Keep individual ledgers, issue receipts, prepare quarterly statements, and reconcile monthly.
Never handle resident money outside this policy, and report any loss or suspected exploitation immediately.

documentation: Written consent for safekeeping and receipts for each deposit or return
Separate written resident ledgers and monthly reconciliation
Quarterly verified statements with resident or representative signature
Surety bond and proof of annual filing with AHCA
Property inventories
Incident reports for loss or suspected misuse
Final accountings at discharge

policies.title: Advance Directives and Do Not Resuscitate Orders
policies.applies_to: Administrator, admissions staff, all direct care staff, and nursing staff
federal: 42 CFR 489.102 (applies only if the facility participates as a provider type subject to it; confirm before relying on it)
policies.purpose: To make sure residents are told about their right to make advance directives and to decline resuscitation, that [AGENCY NAME] never requires a Do Not Resuscitate Order (DNRO) for admission, and that staff know exactly what to do in a cardiac or respiratory arrest.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a)11., F.A.C.: it is the facility policy concerning Do Not Resuscitate Orders under s. 429.255, F.S., and Rule 59A-36.009, F.A.C., and advance directives under Chapter 765, F.S. It is part of the admission package and the resident contract (RR-03, ADM-02). [AGENCY NAME] does not require a DNRO, or any advance directive, as a condition of admission or continued residency. At or before admission, the facility gives each resident (and representative) Form SCHS-4-2006 (or an equivalent) and DH Form 1896, and explains the facility's policy on them. The facility records in the resident record whether DH Form 1896 has been executed. An executed DNRO (DH Form 1896) is honored. If a resident is receiving hospice services, hospice procedures take precedence in a cardiac or respiratory arrest (HS-07). Facilities with 17 or more beds keep a working automated external defibrillator (AED) on the premises as required by s. 429.255, F.S. Residents' choices about advance directives and DNROs are respected and are never used to limit other care or services.

definitions.definition: A written or oral statement of a person's wishes about medical treatment, or the designation of a health care surrogate, made under Chapter 765, F.S.
A physician's order, on DH Form 1896, that CPR is not to be started if the person's breathing or heart stops.
The Florida Department of Health form used to document a DNRO.
The form (or its equivalent) given to residents at admission as required by Rule 59A-36.009, F.A.C.
Automated external defibrillator, a device that analyzes heart rhythm and delivers a shock when indicated.

procedures: During pre-admission and admission, admissions staff tell the resident (and representative) that a DNRO or advance directive is the resident's choice, is not a condition of admission, and will not change the care the resident receives.

At or before admission, admissions staff give the resident (and representative) Form SCHS-4-2006 (or an equivalent) and DH Form 1896, and a copy of this policy. Delivery is recorded in the admission package checklist (ADM-02).

Admissions staff ask whether the resident has an advance directive (living will, health care surrogate designation) or an executed DH Form 1896, and request a copy for the record. The resident is not pressured to complete any document.

If the resident has an executed DH Form 1896, staff file it at the front of the resident record, and record in the record that the form is executed, with the date and the physician. If no form is executed, staff record that DH Form 1896 is not executed.

If the resident has a health care surrogate or other advance directive, the Administrator files a copy and records the surrogate's name and contact information in the record and on the emergency face sheet.
The care plan and the resident's face sheet note the existence of a DNRO or advance directive, and where the original is kept, so any staff member on any shift can find it quickly.

If a resident asks for help in completing an advance directive or DNRO, the Administrator refers the resident to his or her physician, health care surrogate, or an attorney. Staff do not give legal or medical advice and do not sign as witnesses where this would be a conflict.

In a cardiac or respiratory arrest, the first staff member on the scene calls 911 (or directs another staff member to), checks the resident's record or room for an executed DH Form 1896, and checks whether the resident is on hospice.
If an executed DH Form 1896 is present for the resident, staff do not start CPR, stay with the resident, and give the form to emergency responders.
If the resident is receiving hospice services, staff follow the hospice's procedures and call the hospice per HS-07 as well as any 911 call that the hospice plan directs.
If there is no executed DNRO and no hospice plan, trained staff start CPR and use the AED (if the facility is required to have one, or has one) until emergency responders arrive.

Staff notify the Administrator, the resident's physician, and the resident's representative as soon as possible after an arrest, and complete an incident report (SAF-02). The Administrator confirms that the DNRO or hospice order was followed.

If a resident revokes or changes a DNRO or advance directive, staff update the record the same day, destroy or mark superseded copies as the physician and rules direct, and update the face sheet and care plan.
For a facility with 17 or more beds, the Administrator keeps a working AED on the premises, assigns a staff member to check it monthly (battery, pads, and indicator), and records the checks.
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually and trains all staff at orientation and annually on locating and honoring DNROs and advance directives (STF-03).
This policy is included in the admission package and the resident contract is updated if the policy changes (RR-03).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the policy, makes sure forms are given at admission, keeps AED ready (17+ beds), and reviews every arrest event.
Give Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent), DH Form 1896, and this policy at admission, and record whether DH Form 1896 is executed.
Know where DNRO and advance directives are kept and follow the arrest procedure.
Issue and revise DNRO orders and hospice plans of care.

documentation: Admission checklist showing delivery of Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent), DH Form 1896, and this policy
Record entry stating whether DH Form 1896 is executed
Copy of executed DH Form 1896 and advance directives or surrogate designation
Incident report for any arrest
AED check log (17+ beds)
Training records

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors, and students at [AGENCY NAME]
