policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets or exceeds the minimum weekly staff hours in Rule 59A-36.010(3), F.A.C., based on the number of residents in the facility: 168 hours per week for 0–5 residents, 212 for 6–15, 253 for 16–25, 294 for 26–35, 335 for 36–45, and the higher bands in the rule table, with 42 additional hours for each 20 residents over 95. These are minimums only. Staffing is increased as the needs of residents require. At 17 or more residents, awake staff are on duty at all hours. At fewer than 17 residents, a staff member is on the premises at all times and is able to respond immediately. At all times, at least one staff member on site has current First Aid and CPR certification. The facility keeps a written 24-hour staffing schedule. Maintenance, clerical and food service-only hours do not count toward the minimums. AHCA may order additional staff if needed. If the facility holds an ECC license, it keeps adequate awake staff at all hours (Rule 59A-36.021, F.A.C.) and employs or contracts a nurse. If it holds an LNS license, it employs or contracts a nurse available as needed (Rule 59A-36.022, F.A.C.).

definitions.definition: The lowest total number of staff hours per week, set by the Rule 59A-36.010 table according to the resident census, that the facility must provide.
A staff member who is awake and on duty on the premises, not sleeping, during the overnight shift.
The staff member designated in writing to be responsible for the facility when the Administrator is not present.
Hours worked by staff who provide direct care, supervision, personal services or resident supervision. Hours of maintenance, clerical and food service-only staff are excluded.

procedures: The Administrator determines the number of residents in the facility each Monday and whenever the census changes, and compares it to the table in Rule 59A-36.010(3). The Administrator records the census, the required minimum hours and the scheduled hours on the weekly staffing worksheet.

The Administrator sets staffing above the minimum when residents' assessed needs (ADM-03), service plans (ADM-04), dementia care (HS-05) or an ECC or LNS license require it. The reasoning is documented in the staffing plan.

The Administrator writes a 24-hour staffing schedule that shows each shift, each employee on duty by name and position, and the person in charge. The schedule is posted or available to staff and surveyors, and the posted schedule is updated when changes occur.

When the census reaches 17 residents, the Administrator makes sure awake staff are scheduled for every overnight hour before the 17th resident is admitted. The shift supervisor checks the overnight roster at the start of each overnight shift.

At fewer than 17 residents, at least one staff member remains on the premises overnight and is immediately available to residents. The Administrator documents how staff are notified of resident needs, such as a call system.

The Administrator makes sure that at least one staff member on duty during every shift has current First Aid and CPR certification (STF-03). The schedule marks these staff, and expired certifications are corrected before the person works unsupervised.

When the Administrator is absent, the Administrator designates in writing a qualified person in charge who meets the requirements of Rule 59A-36.010. For an extended absence, the Administrator takes the steps the rule requires, including any notice to AHCA. The Administrator also notifies AHCA of an administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006.

Managers are appointed in writing. An Administrator who serves more than one facility may not exceed the limit in the rule (up to 3 facilities) and must make sure each facility has adequate supervision.
Only qualifying hours are counted toward the minimums. Payroll and the staffing worksheet separate hours worked by maintenance, clerical and food service-only staff, and these are not counted.

If a staffing agency or contract staff are used, the Administrator signs a written contract and keeps it on file. Contract staff must pass Level 2 background screening, have the required health and TB documentation, and have the required training before working with residents (STF-02, STF-03, STF-04).

If the facility holds an ECC license, the Administrator confirms there is a nurse on staff or under contract and adequate awake staff at all hours. If it holds an LNS license, the Administrator confirms a nurse is employed or contracted and available as needed (HS-03, HS-09).

Shift supervisors call in replacement staff or use on-call staff when a shift is short. They notify the Administrator immediately if the facility cannot meet the schedule, and the Administrator takes steps to restore it.

The Administrator reviews the staffing worksheet and time records weekly to confirm that the minimum hours were met. Any shortfall is made up in the same week where possible and is documented with the cause and corrective action.
The Administrator reviews staffing quarterly in QA (GOV-03) against incidents, falls, complaints, resident acuity and census trends. The Administrator adjusts staffing when indicated.
If AHCA orders additional staff, the Administrator complies by the date set, documents the change, and keeps the order and response on file.
Staffing schedules, time records and worksheets are kept as required by REC-01 and STF-05 and are available to AHCA surveyors on request.

responsibilities.duty: Calculates required hours, writes the 24-hour schedule, ensures awake overnight staff and First Aid/CPR coverage, designates the person in charge and complies with AHCA staffing orders.
Confirms the roster, CPR/First Aid coverage and awake status each shift, and escalates shortages.
Provides nursing services as required by the license and advises on staffing for resident acuity.
Keeps time records and separates non-qualifying hours.
Report as scheduled, stay awake and on the premises on shift, and hand off resident information.

documentation: Weekly staffing worksheet showing census, required minimum hours and scheduled hours
Written 24-hour staffing schedule
Time and payroll records, with non-qualifying hours separated
Written designation of person in charge and managers
First Aid/CPR certification roster
Contracts with staffing agencies
Notice of administrator change (AHCA Form 3180-1006)
Records of shortages and corrective actions
AHCA staffing orders and responses

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Owners, the administrator, managers, all employees, and contracted or agency staff of [AGENCY NAME]; the Administrator and the human resources designee carry out the procedures.
policies.purpose: To make sure that no person with a disqualifying offense owns, manages, works in, or provides contracted services at the facility, and that Level 2 screening is completed, shared through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse, and kept current.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires Level 2 background screening through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse for all owners, the administrator, and all staff, including contracted staff and staff supplied by staffing agencies, as required by s. 429.174, F.S., s. 408.809, F.S., s. 435.12, F.S., and Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C. Screening results are shared through the Clearinghouse. No person starts work until the Clearinghouse shows the person is eligible or has received an exemption. Each person is rescreened every 5 years, as s. 408.809, F.S. requires. Written contracts are required with every staffing agency that supplies staff. [AGENCY NAME] also applies the agency practices described in this policy, such as license verification and exclusion-list checks, to support safe hiring. The Clearinghouse help line is 850-412-4503.

definitions.definition: A fingerprint-based state and national criminal history check, with review for disqualifying offenses, required by Florida law for owners, the administrator, and staff of an ALF.
The AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. It stores screening results and lets employers share them and receive notices of arrests.
Any individual who works in the facility under a contract or through a staffing agency, rather than as a direct employee.
A repeat Level 2 screening completed at least every 5 years.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Background Screening Coordinator in writing ([NAME/TITLE]) and keeps the facility's Clearinghouse account active and current.
Before an offer of employment or a contract becomes final, the Coordinator tells the applicant that employment depends on a Level 2 screening and on an eligible result in the Clearinghouse.

Each owner, the administrator, and each new employee completes the fingerprint submission with an approved electronic fingerprinting vendor, using [AGENCY NAME]'s facility identifier. The Coordinator records the date submitted.
The Coordinator links each screened person to the facility in the Clearinghouse, so that the facility receives the results and any later arrest notices.

The Coordinator checks the Clearinghouse before the first day of work and prints or saves the result. The person does not begin work, shadow staff, or have resident contact until the result shows 'eligible' or an exemption has been granted.

If a person is found ineligible, the Administrator does not hire or retain that person unless the person has received an exemption from the agency authorized to grant it. The decision and the date are recorded.

Contracted and agency staff: the Administrator signs a written contract with each staffing agency before any agency staff member works in the facility. The contract requires the agency to ensure Level 2 screening and requires each assigned individual to be linked to the facility in the Clearinghouse.

Before an agency staff member's first shift, the Coordinator confirms the individual's eligible status in the Clearinghouse and keeps a copy of the result with the agency contract. Agency staff are not left unsupervised until this is done.
The Coordinator keeps a screening tracker that lists each person, the date screened, the Clearinghouse result, and the date the 5-year rescreen is due.
The Coordinator starts rescreening at least 90 days before each 5-year due date and confirms the new eligible result before the old one expires.

Employees must tell the Administrator within one business day of any arrest or charge, or any change in eligibility, that occurs after hire. The Coordinator also reviews Clearinghouse arrest notices as they are received and reports them to the Administrator the same day.

As an agency practice, before hire the Coordinator verifies any professional license or certification the person claims (for example, nurse, CNA, or HHA) through the Florida Department of Health license lookup. The Coordinator also checks the federal OIG exclusion list. Both results are placed in the personnel file.
When Clearinghouse access problems or questions come up, the Coordinator calls the Clearinghouse help line at 850-412-4503 and records the call, date, and outcome.
On separation, the Coordinator ends the person's link to the facility in the Clearinghouse the same week and notes the date in the tracker.
The Administrator reviews the tracker monthly and certifies in writing that every owner, administrator, employee, and contracted staff member working in the facility has a current eligible result.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that no person works without an eligible Level 2 result, signs staffing agency contracts, reviews the screening tracker monthly, and decides on ineligible results.
Manages the Clearinghouse account, submits screenings, checks results, tracks 5-year rescreens, and files documentation.
Complete their own screening and rescreening and report any arrest or change in eligibility.
Ensures that each assigned worker has an eligible Level 2 result and is linked to the facility in the Clearinghouse.

documentation: Clearinghouse eligibility result for each owner, administrator, employee, and contracted staff member, filed before the first work day.
Screening tracker showing screening dates and 5-year rescreen due dates.
Written contracts with each staffing agency.
License and exclusion-list verifications.
Records of any exemption, ineligibility decision, or arrest report.
Monthly Administrator certification of screening status.

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: All employees and contracted staff of [AGENCY NAME], the Administrator, and managers; the Administrator oversees and the Training Coordinator carries out the procedures.
policies.purpose: To make sure that every staff member is oriented before resident contact and completes the training that Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C. and s. 429.52, F.S. require, including the training needed for extended congregate care, limited mental health, and dementia care.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires only qualified, screened staff and trains them as required by Rule 59A-36.011, F.A.C. and s. 429.52, F.S. Every new staff member completes a 2-hour preservice orientation before any resident contact. Staff must complete 1 hour of infection control training before providing personal care. Within 30 days of hire, staff complete 1 hour on adverse incidents and emergency procedures, 1 hour on resident rights and abuse, and 3 hours on behavior and ADLs, plus training on elopement and HIV/AIDS. Staff who assist with medications complete a 6-hour medication assistance course and 2 hours of continuing education every year. First Aid and CPR, with skills demonstration, are required as described below. Core training with the competency test, continuing education, and any special training required for ECC, LMH, or ADRD care are completed on the schedule in this policy.

definitions.definition: A 2-hour orientation completed before a new staff member has any contact with residents.
The 26-hour core training required of the administrator (and managers, as the rule requires), followed by a competency test that must be passed with at least 75%.

The topic-based training required for staff, covering infection control, adverse incidents and emergency procedures, resident rights and abuse, behavior and ADLs, safe food handling, elopement, and HIV/AIDS.
The 6-hour course required for staff who assist residents with self-administration of medications, plus 2 hours of continuing education each year.

Additional training required of staff in facilities holding an Extended Congregate Care or Limited Mental Health license, and of staff who care for residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders.

procedures: Before offering a job, the Administrator confirms the applicant's identity, references, and qualifications. The applicant must have an eligible Level 2 result under STF-02 before starting.

On or before the first day, the Training Coordinator gives each new employee the job description and the facility's policies on resident rights, abuse reporting, and emergency procedures, and obtains the employee's signed receipt.
Before any resident contact, the employee completes the 2-hour preservice orientation. The Training Coordinator signs and dates the attendance record.
Before the employee provides any personal care, the employee completes 1 hour of infection control training. Until the training is documented, the employee does not perform personal care.

Within 30 days of hire, the employee completes 1 hour on adverse incidents and emergency procedures, 1 hour on resident rights and abuse, and 3 hours on behavior and ADLs. The employee also completes training on elopement and HIV/AIDS. The Training Coordinator records each date and the trainer.

The administrator, and any manager appointed in writing, complete the 26-hour core training and pass the competency test (75%) within the period Rule 59A-36.011 requires: within 90 days for the administrator, and within 3 months for staff otherwise required. Test results are filed.
The administrator completes 12 hours of continuing education every 2 years. The Training Coordinator tracks the due date and schedules courses at least 90 days ahead.

Staff who will assist residents with medications are not assigned this duty until they have completed the 6-hour medication assistance course. Each such staff member then completes 2 hours of continuing education annually. See HS-02.

Each staff member who has hands-on contact completes First Aid and CPR with an in-person skills demonstration. The Training Coordinator keeps the card or certificate and the expiration date. The Administrator ensures that at least one staff member with current CPR and First Aid is present at all times (see STF-01).
Staff who prepare or serve food complete safe food handling training, and the food service continuing education the rule requires. See DL-01.

Staff who care for residents with dementia complete the ADRD training required by rule (see HS-05). If the facility holds an ECC license (HS-09, HS-10) or an LMH license (HS-11), the staff assigned to those residents complete the ECC or LMH training the rules require before working with these residents.

The Training Coordinator keeps a training matrix that shows every staff member, each required course, the date completed, and the date the next course is due. The Administrator reviews the matrix at least monthly.
Trainers must be qualified as the rule requires. The Training Coordinator keeps the trainer's name and credentials with each record.
Each staff member's competency in resident care tasks is observed and signed off by a supervisor within 30 days of hire and reviewed at least annually.
Staff who fail the competency test or miss a required course are removed from the affected duties until the requirement is met. The Administrator documents the corrective plan and date.
Staff may be given additional training after an incident, a survey finding, or a quality assurance review (see GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that all training is completed on time, completes own core training and continuing education, and approves duty assignments only after training is documented.
Schedules and documents orientation and in-service training, maintains the training matrix, and files certificates.
Observe and sign off on staff competency, and do not assign untrained staff to restricted tasks.
Attend assigned training, pass required tests, and maintain current CPR and First Aid.

documentation: Preservice orientation and infection control attendance records, dated before first resident contact and before personal care.
30-day in-service training records (adverse incidents and emergencies, resident rights and abuse, behavior/ADLs, elopement, HIV/AIDS).
Core training certificates and competency test results.
Medication assistance course certificates and annual continuing education records.
First Aid/CPR certificates with skills demonstration.
Food handler and food service continuing education records.
ECC, LMH, and ADRD training records.
Training matrix and competency checklists in each personnel file.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees and contracted staff of [AGENCY NAME], including the Administrator; the Administrator and the personnel records designee carry out the procedures.
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease by documenting each staff member's health status at hire and annual tuberculosis (TB) screening, as Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C. requires, and by providing protections for staff exposed to blood and other infectious materials.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires a staff health statement for every staff member within 30 days of hire and annual TB documentation, as required by Rule 59A-36.010, F.A.C. These records are kept in the personnel file. Staff with a communicable disease or TB symptoms do not work until cleared by a health care provider. [AGENCY NAME] also follows the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030, for staff with occupational exposure.

definitions.definition: A statement signed by a health care provider (or other person the rule allows) that the staff member is free of signs and symptoms of communicable disease and is able to perform assigned duties, obtained within 30 days of hire.
Documentation each year that the staff member has been screened for TB and is free of active TB disease, as the rule requires.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious materials during assigned duties, as defined in 29 CFR 1910.1030.

procedures: At the job offer, the personnel records designee tells the applicant that a health statement is due within 30 days of hire and that TB screening documentation is required each year.
The designee gives the new employee the facility's health statement form (or accepts the practitioner's equivalent form) and a TB screening instruction sheet on or before the first day of work.
The designee records the hire date and the 30-day due date on the health tracker. The completed health statement is filed in the personnel file within 30 days of hire.

TB screening documentation is obtained as the rule requires at hire and at least annually thereafter. The designee records the date and the result and files the report. Documentation is accepted only from a licensed provider, the county health department, or another source the rule allows.
If an employee has not provided the health statement by day 30, the Administrator removes the employee from the schedule until it is received, and records the action.

If a screening result is positive or the employee reports TB symptoms (persistent cough, fever, night sweats, weight loss), the employee does not work until a health care provider or the county health department clears the employee in writing. The Administrator contacts the county health department as directed.

Staff must report any communicable illness (for example, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, or fever) to the supervisor before the shift. Staff with symptoms do not provide resident care, handle food, or work in resident areas until cleared. See SAF-13.
The designee tracks every annual TB due date and sends the employee a written reminder at least 30 days ahead. Staff whose documentation expires are not scheduled until it is current.

For staff with occupational exposure, the Administrator offers the hepatitis B vaccine at no cost within 10 working days of assignment, as 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires, and documents acceptance or a signed declination.
The Administrator provides bloodborne pathogen training to exposed staff at assignment and annually, and makes personal protective equipment available at no cost.

After an exposure incident (needlestick, splash, or other contact), the employee immediately washes the area, reports to the supervisor, and receives a confidential medical evaluation and follow-up at no cost. The incident is recorded under SAF-02.
Employee health information is kept confidential and in the personnel file, kept separate from resident records, and is shared only with persons who need it.
Contracted and agency staff must provide the same health statement and TB documentation, which the designee files with the agency contract. Agency contracts require the agency to maintain them.
The Administrator reviews the health tracker monthly and records the review.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that health statements and TB documentation are complete, removes noncompliant staff from the schedule, and manages exposure follow-up.
Issues forms, tracks due dates, files documentation, and sends reminders.
Send staff home if they have symptoms of illness and report to the Administrator.
Complete screening on time and report illness, symptoms, and exposure incidents promptly.

documentation: Signed staff health statement in each personnel file, dated within 30 days of hire.
Annual TB documentation with dates and source.
Health tracker with due dates and monthly Administrator review.
Hepatitis B vaccination acceptance or declination forms.
Bloodborne pathogen training attendance records.
Exposure incident reports and medical follow-up records (kept confidential).
Work clearance letters after illness or positive screening.

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All personnel files for employees, the administrator, managers, and contracted staff of [AGENCY NAME]; the Administrator and the personnel records designee carry out the procedures.
policies.purpose: To maintain a complete, current, and secure personnel record for each staff member, as Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C. and s. 429.275, F.S. require, and to have these records ready for AHCA inspection at the facility address.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel record for every staff member that contains screening, training, license, and health records. Training certificates and continuing education hours are tracked. All personnel records are kept at the facility address at [ADDRESS] and are available to AHCA surveyors during inspections, as Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C. requires. Personnel records are kept confidential and are accessible only to the Administrator and designated staff.

definitions.definition: The file for each staff member containing hire, screening, training, license, health, and performance documents.
Able to be produced at the facility address on request during an inspection, without delay.

procedures: The personnel records designee opens a personnel file for every new employee, and for each contracted staff member who regularly works at the facility, on or before the first day of work.

Each file contains: application and résumé; job description; proof of identity; Level 2 screening and Clearinghouse eligibility result (STF-02); staff health statement and annual TB documentation (STF-04); training records and certificates (STF-03); First Aid/CPR card; and a copy of any professional license or certification, with its expiration date.

For staff who assist with medications, the file also holds the medication assistance course certificate and annual continuing education records. For administrators and managers, the file holds the core training certificate, competency test result, and 12-hour continuing education records.
For ECC, LMH, and ADRD staff assignments, the file holds the specialized training records required for those assignments.

The file also includes signed acknowledgments of resident rights and abuse reporting responsibilities, the confidentiality agreement, performance evaluations, disciplinary notes, and any incident reports involving the staff member.
For contracted and agency staff, the designee files the written staffing agency contract and proof of Level 2 screening, health documentation, and training supplied by the agency.

The designee maintains a training and credentials tracker that shows each license or certification, the CE hours completed, and the next due dates. The tracker is reviewed monthly by the Administrator.
Files are kept at the facility address in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Records kept electronically must be printable and accessible at the facility during an inspection.
During an AHCA inspection, the Administrator or the person in charge gives the surveyor the files requested without delay and keeps a list of the files shown.
Each quarter, the designee audits at least one-quarter of the files against a checklist of required contents, and the Administrator signs the audit. Missing items are corrected within 14 days.
Employee health and background screening information is kept confidential. Only the Administrator, the designee, and authorized regulators have access.
Employees may review their own files by request in the presence of the designee. They may not remove documents.
[AGENCY NAME] keeps each personnel file for at least five years after the staff member's separation, unless a longer period is required by law, and then destroys it securely.
A separated employee's file is moved to inactive storage on the same schedule, and the date of separation and reason are noted on the cover sheet.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that all required records are present and current, certifies the quarterly audits, and produces records at inspection.
Builds and maintains files, updates the training and credentials tracker, and secures records.
Provide current licenses, certificates, and health documents on time.

documentation: Complete personnel file for each staff member and contracted worker.
Training and credentials tracker.
Quarterly personnel file audit checklist signed by the Administrator.
Log of records requested and produced at inspection.
Separation date and secure destruction record.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, managers, the Administrator, owners, volunteers, and contracted staff of [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To protect residents' rights, funds, and property, to set clear professional boundaries, and to ensure that staff are paid lawfully, as required by the resident Bill of Rights (s. 429.28, F.S.), Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C., and the Florida minimum wage provision.
policies.policy: Staff of [AGENCY NAME] treat every resident with dignity and respect and honor the resident Bill of Rights under s. 429.28, F.S. Residents may not be required to perform work for the facility without compensation, as Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C. provides. Staff may not misuse a resident's funds or property. Staff maintain professional boundaries and report any violation. [AGENCY NAME] pays every employee at or above the Florida minimum wage, which is $14.00 per hour from September 30, 2025 and $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026 (Fla. Const. Art. X, s. 24).

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a staff member's professional relationship with a resident from a personal, financial, or romantic relationship.
Using, borrowing, accepting, or taking a resident's money or belongings for any purpose other than the resident's own benefit and consent.

Work for the facility or its staff performed by a resident without pay. A resident may not be required to do it. Residents may choose tasks, such as helping with personal items, only as the Bill of Rights and Rule 59A-36.007 allow.

procedures: At hire and annually, every staff member reads and signs the Code of Conduct, which is based on this policy, and attends training on resident rights, abuse, and boundaries (STF-03).
Staff address residents by their preferred names, knock before entering rooms, protect privacy during personal care, and follow resident choices as the Bill of Rights requires (RR-01).

No staff member may require or pressure a resident to perform work for the facility, staff, or owners without pay. If a resident volunteers for a task or activity, the Administrator documents that the choice was voluntary and that the resident was not penalized for declining.
Staff may not borrow money from, sell to, or buy from residents, and may not use a resident's property, vehicle, phone, or accounts for personal benefit.

Staff may not accept gifts of money, or gifts of significant value, from residents or families. A staff member who is offered a gift tells the supervisor, who decides on a case-by-case basis and records the decision. Small tokens such as food or cards may be accepted if the Administrator approves.

Staff may not hold a resident's money, bank card, or valuables, or serve as agent, power of attorney, trustee, or beneficiary of a resident, unless the Administrator has approved in writing and the law permits. Resident funds are handled only under RR-04.

Staff may not engage in romantic or sexual relationships with residents, or use social media, text, or private contact to form a personal relationship with a resident or family member outside work duties.
Staff may not discuss resident information outside work or post any resident photos or information on social media (RR-06).

Staff may not use threats, retaliation, or restriction of services against a resident or family member who makes a complaint. Retaliation against a staff member who reports a concern is also prohibited (RR-02).

Staff must report any suspected abuse, neglect, or exploitation immediately to the Administrator and to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, as SAF-01 provides. Failure to report is cause for discipline.

Staff who see or learn of misuse of resident funds or property, a boundary violation, or uncompensated resident work report it to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator starts an investigation within 24 hours and documents the findings.
During an investigation, the Administrator may reassign the staff member away from the resident involved or suspend the staff member.
Confirmed violations lead to discipline up to and including termination, and to reports to licensing boards, law enforcement, or AHCA as the law requires.

The Administrator verifies at hire and at each wage change that every employee's hourly pay is at or above the Florida minimum wage: $14.00 per hour from September 30, 2025, and $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026. The Administrator reviews payroll before each effective date and records the review.
Staff are paid for all hours worked, including orientation and training time, and are not required to work off the clock.

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the Code of Conduct, investigates reports, ensures that wages meet the minimum wage, and reports as the law requires.
Model professional conduct, monitor boundaries, and escalate concerns on the same day.
Follow the Code of Conduct, protect residents' rights, funds, and property, and report violations and suspected abuse.
Do not direct or allow uncompensated resident work or misuse of resident property, and fund payroll at lawful wage levels.

documentation: Signed Code of Conduct acknowledgments for each staff member.
Training records on resident rights, abuse, and boundaries.
Gift and boundary concern reports and Administrator decisions.
Investigation files and disciplinary records.
Payroll review records showing compliance with the minimum wage.
Records of voluntary resident activities, if any, showing voluntary participation.

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All resident records, in paper or electronic form, maintained by [AGENCY NAME]; the Administrator and the records designee carry out the procedures.
policies.purpose: To create, protect, retain, and produce resident records as required by Rule 59A-36.015, F.A.C., including resident contracts under Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C. and admission and exam records under Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete record for each resident and keeps these records at the licensee's physical address at [ADDRESS], where they are readily available for inspection. Resident contracts are retained for 5 years. Other resident records are retained for 2 years after the resident's departure. [AGENCY NAME] maintains an admission and discharge log. Resident records are kept confidential and protected under the HIPAA privacy requirements of 45 CFR 164.530 and RR-06.

definitions.definition: All documents about a resident, including the admission paperwork, health information, assessments, service plans, medication records, and incident notes.
A running log of the date each resident was admitted and the date and reason each resident was discharged or left the facility.
The written contract offered to each resident before or at admission, as required by Rule 59A-36.018, F.A.C.
Kept at the facility address and able to be produced to authorized persons and AHCA surveyors on request.

procedures: The records designee opens a record for each resident on the day of admission and enters the resident in the admission and discharge log with the admission date. The date and reason for any later discharge, transfer, or death are entered in the log the same day.

Each record contains the signed resident contract and any addenda (RR-03; Rule 59A-36.018), the admission package items the resident received (ADM-02), and a copy of the pre-admission screening (ADM-01).

Each record contains the face-to-face medical examination on AHCA Form 1823 or the practitioner's equivalent form, completed within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, and the exam updates required at least every 3 years or after a significant change (ADM-03; Rule 59A-36.006).
Each record contains the resident assessment and service plan with updates (ADM-03, ADM-04), medication orders and records (HS-01, HS-02), and any advance directive or DNRO (RR-05).

Each record contains the written record of significant changes in condition and physician or practitioner notifications (HS-04), incident reports involving the resident (SAF-02), third-party service provider information (hospice, home health), and any ECC, LMH, or specialty documentation that applies.

Each record contains the resident's emergency contacts, designated representative, and notices of rate increases or other changes given to the resident in writing, and the resident's grievance filings, if any (RR-02).

The Administrator keeps the facility records required by Rule 59A-36.015, including the admission and discharge log, required policies, inspection reports, and the license on display, at the facility address where AHCA may review them.

Resident records are kept in a locked cabinet or in a password-protected electronic system. Access is limited to staff who need the information to do their jobs, and each person with access signs the confidentiality agreement (RR-06).
Electronic records may be used if they are backed up and can be printed at the facility on request, so that they are available at the facility address during inspection.

Staff may not remove original records from the facility, except to comply with a legal order. Copies may be sent with a resident transferred to a hospital or another provider, as HS-04 and ADM-06 provide, and the transfer is noted in the record.

Residents and their authorized representatives may review their record by request. The designee provides access within a reasonable time and in a manner that protects other residents' information, and logs any copies given.
Resident contracts are kept for 5 years. The retention date is calculated from the contract's date and noted on the record cover sheet.

All other resident records are kept for 2 years after the resident's departure date. [AGENCY NAME] may keep them longer if a longer period is needed because of litigation, a pending complaint or investigation, or the Administrator's judgment. HIPAA-required documentation, such as privacy policies and complaint records, is kept for the period set in 45 CFR 164.530 and RR-06.

When a resident leaves, the designee completes the discharge entry in the log, places the record in closed storage, labeled with the discharge date and destruction date, and keeps it locked at the facility address.

After the retention period ends, and after confirming that no legal hold applies, the Administrator approves destruction. Records are shredded or erased securely and a destruction log is kept with the date, the resident name or number, and the approver.
During inspections, the Administrator or the person in charge produces records on request and notes which records were reviewed.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures that records are complete, kept at the facility address, protected, retained for the required period, and produced for inspections; approves destruction.
Opens and files records, keeps the admission and discharge log, applies retention dates, and manages access.
Document accurately and promptly, protect confidentiality, and do not remove or alter records improperly.

documentation: Admission and discharge log.
Resident record for each current and former resident.
Resident contracts with retention dates.
Medical examination form (AHCA Form 1823 or equivalent) and updates.
Records access log and confidentiality agreements.
Record destruction log.
Inspection record showing which records were produced.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designee, owner/governing body, and all staff who prepare, submit or file reports with AHCA, county emergency management or other regulators; applies to the standard license and to any ECC, LNS or LMH specialty license held by the facility.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] submits every required report, notice, application and plan update to the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA), county emergency management and other regulators on time, accurately and in the required manner, and keeps proof of each submission.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will file all reports and notices required of a Florida assisted living facility, on the required form and by the required deadline, and will keep a copy and proof of submission at the licensed address. The Administrator is accountable for the reporting calendar. The facility will not represent or advertise any service beyond its license and will not change licensed capacity or convert space to resident use without the prior approval required by Rule 59A-36.004, F.A.C. (C1). Deadlines covered by this policy are: copies of annual fire and sanitation inspections to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days; notice of an Administrator change to AHCA within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006; the annual Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) to the county, with significant modifications submitted within 30 days (Rule 59A-36.019, C12); evacuation reporting within 6 hours; the 48-hour report when sheltering evacuees above licensed capacity; and license renewal filed online at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-35.060, C33). Reports are kept as records under Rule 59A-36.015 (C10). This policy does not replace the incident, abuse or death reporting rules in the related policies. It provides the calendar and filing control that supports them.

definitions.definition: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration, Bureau of Health Facility Regulation, Assisted Living Unit, which licenses and surveys assisted living facilities. Phone (850) 412-4304; email assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com.
AHCA's Tallahassee-based Assisted Living Unit (Central Office) and the AHCA field office serving the facility's area (Field Office). Each receives different submissions, as stated in this policy.
The facility's written Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan, prepared on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023) and approved by the county emergency management agency.

A change to the CEMP that alters how the plan operates (for example, evacuation destination, transportation arrangements, key contacts or sheltering approach), as opposed to a typographical correction. The Administrator decides and documents whether a change is significant. When in doubt, the change is treated as significant.
The facility's written log of every recurring and event-driven report, its due date, the responsible person, the date submitted and the proof of submission.
A resident whose care or room and board is paid in whole or part through a state program such as Medicaid long-term care or Optional State Supplementation.

procedures: Reporting calendar: By the first day the facility operates, the Administrator creates and thereafter maintains a Reporting Calendar listing each report in this policy, its deadline, the person responsible, and a backup person. The calendar is reviewed at the start of each month and at the quarterly QA meeting (GOV-03).

Inspection reports: When the local fire authority or county health department completes the annual fire or sanitation inspection, the Administrator or designee logs the inspection date the day the report is received and sets a reminder for 20 days after the inspection.

Within 30 calendar days of each annual fire inspection and each annual sanitation inspection, the Administrator sends a copy of the report to the AHCA Central Office, and files a dated copy with proof of submission (email confirmation or mailing record) in the Regulatory Reports file. The Administrator does not wait for the 30th day. Any deficiency noted is also entered in the maintenance and QA logs (DL-03, GOV-03).

Administrator change: If the Administrator resigns, is terminated or is replaced, the owner or governing body notifies AHCA within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006. The outgoing Administrator or the owner signs and submits the form. A copy is filed in the Regulatory Reports file and in the governing body records (GOV-01). The facility makes sure a qualified Administrator or designee is in charge during any transition.

Capacity and space changes: Before increasing or decreasing licensed capacity, the owner submits the request to AHCA Central Office and waits for written approval. Before any space not previously inspected is converted to resident use, the owner requests approval from the AHCA Field Office and waits for written approval. The facility does not occupy or market the beds or space until approval is on file. Approvals are kept in the Regulatory Reports file.

Scope of services: Before any marketing material, website, contract or brochure is issued, the Administrator confirms it does not describe or imply any service beyond the facility's license (standard, ECC, LNS or LMH). Any correction is made immediately and documented.
Buildings under one license: The owner confirms that all buildings operated under this license are on contiguous property. No building on non-contiguous property is added to the license.

Annual CEMP: Each year, on the schedule shown on the Reporting Calendar, the Administrator reviews the CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006, updates it, and submits it to the county emergency management agency for approval (SAF-05). The Administrator retains the transmittal and the county's written approval.

CEMP modifications: When a significant modification is made to the CEMP, the Administrator submits it to the county emergency management agency within 30 days of the change and keeps proof of submission. Staff are informed of the change and training records are updated (STF-03).
CEMP training: The Administrator verifies that every new employee is trained on the CEMP within 30 days of hire and that the training is recorded in the personnel file (STF-03, STF-05).

Evacuation report: If the facility evacuates residents, the Administrator or the person in charge reports the evacuation to the required agency within 6 hours of the evacuation and records the time and the person notified. The report is made before any non-urgent paperwork is done. A written copy or confirmation is filed with the emergency event record (SAF-07).

Emergency shelter above capacity: If the facility accepts evacuees from another facility and exceeds licensed capacity, the Administrator keeps the required log of evacuees and submits the required report within 48 hours. The report and log are filed in the emergency event record (SAF-08).

License renewal: At least 90 days before license expiration, the Administrator confirms the expiration date, fees due, and any changes in ownership, capacity or specialty licenses. The online renewal application is filed through AHCA's online licensing portal at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-35.060). Paper renewal is not used. The confirmation page and fee payment receipt are saved in the Regulatory Reports file. Any change that requires a different application (for example change of ownership or adding ECC, LNS or LMH) is submitted separately and not by renewal.

State-funded residents: When AHCA asks which residents are state-funded, the Administrator or business office provides a current list from the resident ledger within the time stated in the request. The list is limited to what is requested and shared in a way that protects confidentiality (RR-06).

Survey and complaint reports: Every AHCA survey report, statement of deficiencies, plan of correction and complaint investigation report is logged on receipt, filed at the licensed address and made available to residents and visitors where required. The plan of correction is submitted by the date stated by AHCA. The Administrator documents the completion of each correction (GOV-02, GOV-03).

Records availability: The Administrator keeps the license on display, the admission/discharge log, required policies and procedures, inspection reports and report copies at the facility's physical address, ready for inspection by AHCA at any time (REC-01). Records are not kept only off-site or only on a corporate server unless immediately retrievable at the facility.

Retention: Resident contracts are kept 5 years. Other resident records are kept 2 years after the resident leaves the facility. Report files are kept at least as long as the facility's retention schedule requires and are not destroyed while a survey, complaint, claim or investigation is open.

Audit and corrections: Each quarter the Administrator reviews the Reporting Calendar against the file copies. A missed or late report is reported to the owner, sent immediately, and documented with the reason and the corrective step in the QA minutes. If the facility is unsure whether a report is required or what a deadline is, the Administrator contacts AHCA at (850) 412-4304 or assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com and records the answer.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the Reporting Calendar; submits or supervises every report in this policy; keeps proof of submission; reviews the calendar monthly and quarterly; and reports late or missed items to the owner.

Signs and files Administrator-change notices within 10 days; requests prior approvals for capacity or space changes; pays licensing fees; reviews QA reports on timeliness of filings.
Maintains the file copies, provides the state-funded resident list on request, and keeps required records at the licensed address.
Notifies the Administrator the day a fire or sanitation inspection occurs and provides the report promptly.

required_items.text: Provision for all hazards;

Provision for the care of residents remaining in the facility during an emergency, including pre-disaster or emergency preparation; protecting the facility; supplies; emergency power; food and water; staffing; and emergency equipment;

Provision for the care of residents who must be evacuated from the facility during an emergency including identification of such residents and transfer of resident records; evacuation transportation; sheltering arrangements; supplies; staffing; emergency equipment; and medications;
Provision for the care of additional residents who may be evacuated to the facility during an emergency including the identification of such residents, staffing, and supplies;
Identification of residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, and residents with mobility limitations who may need specialized assistance either at the facility or in case of evacuation;
Identification of and coordination with the county emergency management agency;

Arrangement for post-disaster activities including responding to family inquiries, obtaining medical intervention for residents, transportation, and reporting to the county emergency management agency the number of residents who have been relocated, and the place of relocation; and,
The identification of staff responsible for implementing each part of the plan.
All staff must be trained in their duties and are responsible for implementing the emergency management plan. New staff must be trained on the plan within 30 days of employment.

The acquisition of a sufficient alternate power source such as a generator(s), maintained at the assisted living facility, to ensure that ... ambient air temperatures will be maintained at or below 81 degrees Fahrenheit for a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours in the event of the loss of primary electrical power. [The plan must include the area(s) where the temperature will be maintained, and the systems and equipment and fuel required to operate them.]

The acquisition of sufficient fuel, and safe maintenance of that fuel at the facility, to ensure that ... there is sufficient fuel available for the alternate power source to maintain ambient temperatures at or below 81 degrees Fahrenheit for a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours ... The plan must include information regarding fuel source and fuel storage.

The acquisition of services necessary to maintain, and test the equipment and its functions to ensure the safe and sufficient operation of the alternate power source maintained at the assisted living facility.
The acquisition and maintenance of a carbon monoxide alarm.

Each assisted living facility shall develop and implement written policies and procedures to ensure that the assisted living facility can effectively and immediately activate, operate and maintain the alternate power source and any fuel required for the operation of the alternate power source. ... Procedures must address the care of residents occupying the facility during a declared state of emergency, specifically, a description of the methods to be used to mitigate the potential for heat related injury including:
The use of cooling devices and equipment;
The use of refrigeration and freezers to produce ice and appropriate temperatures for the maintenance of medicines requiring refrigeration;
Wellness checks by assisted living facility staff to monitor for signs of dehydration and heat injury; and
A provision for obtaining medical intervention from emergency services for residents whose life safety is in jeopardy.

The facility's admission policy and the services the facility is prepared to provide or arrange in order to meet resident needs. [Basis for the administrator's appropriateness-of-admission determination.]
The facility's admission and continued residency criteria;
The daily, weekly or monthly charge to reside in the facility and the services, supplies, and accommodations provided by the facility for that rate;
Personal care services that the facility is prepared to provide to residents and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Nursing services that the facility is prepared to provide to residents and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Food service and the ability of the facility to accommodate special diets;
The availability of transportation and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Any other special services that are provided by the facility and additional cost if any;
Social and leisure activities generally offered by the facility;
Any services that the facility does not provide but will arrange for the resident and additional cost, if any;
The facility rules and regulations that residents must follow as described in Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C.;
The facility policy concerning Do Not Resuscitate Orders pursuant to Section 429.255, F.S., and Rule 59A-36.009, F.A.C., and Advance Directives pursuant to Chapter 765, F.S.;

If the facility is licensed to provide extended congregate care, the facility's residency criteria for residents receiving extended congregate care services. The facility must also provide a description of the additional personal, supportive, and nursing services provided by the facility including additional costs and any limitations on where extended congregate care residents may reside based on the policies and procedures described in Rule 59A-36.021, F.A.C.;

If the facility advertises that it provides special care for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders, a written description of those special services as required in Section 429.177, F.S.; and,
The facility's resident elopement response policies and procedures.
All trained staff must adhere to the facility's infection control policy and procedures when assisting with the self-administration of medication.

The facility's rules and regulations require central storage of medication and that policy has been provided to the resident before admission as required in Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C. [Medication central-storage policy, if the facility has one.]
Aging in place; [ECC only: the facility must develop and implement specific written policies and procedures that address:]
The facility's residency criteria developed in accordance with the admission and discharge requirements described in subsection (4), and extended congregate care services listed in subsection (7);

The personal and supportive services the facility intends to provide, how the services will be provided, and the identification of staff positions to provide the services including their relationship to the facility;

The nursing services the facility intends to provide, identification of staff positions to provide nursing services, and the license status, duties, general working hours, and supervision of such staff;
Identifying potential unscheduled resident service needs and mechanisms for meeting those needs including the identification of resources to meet those needs;
A process for mediating conflicts among residents regarding choice of room or apartment and roommate; and,

How to involve residents in decisions concerning the resident. The services must provide opportunities and encouragement for the resident to make personal choices and decisions. If a resident needs assistance to make choices or decisions, a family member or other resident representative must be consulted. Choices must include at a minimum whether:
To participate in the process of developing, implementing, reviewing, and revising the resident's service plan,

To remain in the same room in the facility, except that a current resident transferring into an extended congregate care services may be required to move to the part of the facility licensed for extended congregate care, if only part of the facility is so licensed,
To select among social and leisure activities,
To participate in activities in the community. At a minimum the facility must arrange transportation to such activities if requested by the resident; and,
To provide input with respect to the adoption and amendment of facility policies and procedures.

official.notes: Florida publishes no single policy-and-procedure checklist for ALF licensure. The AHCA ALF page lists none, and the application is filed through the AHCA online licensing system. The items above therefore come from the rule sections that list written content. Every item is quoted from the Cornell LII copy of the F.A.C. text, whose notes show the amendment dates in each document's version field. Compare against the official Florida Administrative Rules Gateway (flrules.org) before relying on it. Organization and submission: (1) The Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan must be written on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept. 2023) and submitted to the county emergency management agency, which is the final administrative authority. A significant modification must be submitted within 30 days (59A-36.019(2)). (2) The emergency power plan under 59A-36.025 supplements the CEMP. A new ALF must submit and implement it before obtaining a license. After county approval, proof of approval must go to AHCA at assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com within 30 days, along with a consumer-friendly summary. AHCA's page offers an Emergency Power Plan Sample Format. The written power policies (59A-36.025(5)) must be kept at the facility, be producible immediately, and be open to residents and their representatives. (3) The 59A-36.006(3) admission statement can be met with the resident contract or a brochure that contains all 14 items. Resident contracts must also meet Rule 59A-36.018, which was not fetched. (4) The ECC policies in 59A-36.021(2) apply only if the facility seeks an ECC license. They must be kept as a record under 59A-36.021(8)(d). LNS (59A-36.022) and LMH (59A-36.020) list no written policy topics. They set staffing, records, and per-resident plans. Not reviewed: Rules 59A-36.007 (facility rules and resident rights), 59A-36.009, 59A-36.010 (staffing), 59A-36.011 (training), 59A-36.012 to 59A-36.018, and ss. 429.28 and 429.41, F.S. These may require further written policies, such as rules and regulations, DNR, resident rights, and abuse reporting. Verify them against the rule text before finalizing the manual. The AHCA ALF survey tags PDF may also be useful, but it was not opened.
